Verdict — 6 of 12 lanes cannot be trusted today

6 lanes refresh on their own. The rest are one-off research snapshots that the Phase-1 freshness rule has already demoted to zero attention. Automating them is the whole of Phase 2; no new signal is added.

  1. TRENDS-ATTN — 90d old against a 14d limit (weekly (archive stale) cadence). Write the collector, schedule it, run the three B3 checks.
  2. FED-ISSUANCE — 58d old against a 45d limit (monthly cadence). Write the collector, schedule it, run the three B3 checks.
  3. ECB-SPEECH-VOL — 20d old against a 14d limit (weekly cadence). Write the collector, schedule it, run the three B3 checks.
  4. Exit test: 10 consecutive unattended days with ≥10 of 12 lanes FRESH. Anything less is not done.

2.1 Data vintage board

Bar is the age of the newest observation; dashed rule is the cadence limit past which the series stops being evidence. Red bars have crossed it.

Welch-Goyal (2008): in-sample fit computed on data that did not exist at the decision time is inadmissible. The dashed rule is where a lane stops being point-in-time and starts being hindsight.

2.2 Collector board

Each lane needs a collector, a schedule, and three separate B3 proofs. A green schedule with no induced-failure test is the state where silent breakage lives.

2.4 Out of scope for this phase

No new signal, no forecast, no ranking change. Phase 2 only makes existing lanes refresh themselves. Adding signals while the refresh path is unproven would grow the multiple-testing denominator with data we cannot re-read tomorrow.
